title: Jinggoy Estrada's 'fees' linked to Bulacan pumping stations, solar lights --witness
summary: Senator Jinggoy Estrada"s P213 million worth of "commitment fees" or “kickbacks” stemmed from P355 million worth of pumping stations and P500 million worth of solar street lights in Bulacan, a…

blocks.text: Senator Jinggoy Estrada’s P213 million worth of "commitment fees" or “kickbacks” stemmed from P355 million worth of pumping stations and P500 million worth of solar street lights in Bulacan, a prosecution witness said Friday.

Carlo Rivera, a former engineer at the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Bulacan First District Engineering Office (DEO), gave testimony during the ongoing hearing on the bail petition filed by Estrada before the Sandiganbayan Fifth Division.
Estrada is facing a P573 million plunder charge over his alleged involvement in the flood control kickback scheme.

“Ang sabi po niya prepare a list for Senator Estrada…iyong P300 million pumping station, i-tag kay SJE,” Rivera said, referring to this former boss, state witness and ex-Bulacan First DEO District Engineer Henry Alcantara.
It was Alcantara who previously told the anti-graft court that Estrada got a 25% commitment fee per project. Alcantara, however, did not specify the nature of these Bulacan projects.
“The total amount of solar street lights is P500 million,” Rivera said.
Another prosecution witness, Edrick San Diego, said he served as a driver for Alcantara but was paid as a lot technician.
Likewise, San Diego said his task was only to deliver the boxes to state witness and the DPWH Undersecretary Roberto Bernardo, not to Estrada.
“Hindi ko alam ano nangyari [sa mga boxes] after madeliver sa Diamond Hotel,” San Diego said.
After San Diego’s testimony, the prosecution informed the Sandiganbayan that San Diego would be its last witness.
As a result, the Sandiganbayan gave the prosecution 10 days to submit its formal offer of evidence. —LDF, GMA News
